page.layout: One column of running text, with two marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines "quasi septa" and "tetarum epi". A catchword at the lower right. The printed page number is at the head, with the running head "DE EPISTOLIS" beside it.

main_text.l: gi ac refutari non possunt. Ac tametsi Cæ-
far libro de Oratore secundo naturæ, non
artis esse facetias affirmet: tamen & natu-
ra iuuatur bona arte atque obseruatione,
&, quod admodum in iocis difficile, intra
quasi septa & cancellos continetur. Et
Cicero quadam ad Volumnium epistola o-
stendit, quibusnam potissimum ex locis
petendi ioci sint. Pugna, inquit, si me a-
mas, nisi acuta ἀμφιβολία [?], nisi elegans
εὐσχολία [?], nisi παράγραμμα [?] bellum, nisi ridiculum
παρὰ προσδοκίαν [?], nisi cætera quæ sunt in se-
cundo libro de Oratore per Antonij per-
sonam disputata de ridiculis, ἐντέχνα [?], & aperte
apparebunt, ut sacramento contenti
das mea non esse. Sumuntur ergo in face-
tiis & iocosis epistolis sententiæ, primùm
ex loco notationis: ab
ἐτυμολογία [?], interpre-
tatione atque explicatione vocabuli,
ὁμωνυμία [?], verbi ambiguitate, εἰρωνεία [?], dissimu-
latione, ἀλληγορείας [?] & translationibus cre-
bris. Deinde ex Adiunctis, & circumstan-
tiis, loci, personarū, temporis, modi, cau-
sarum, quæ occasiones atque causas iocis
præbent. Tertiò Testimoniis & sermonibus
partim hominum, partim sententiis
ac dictis præclarorum virorum, in quibus
singularis esse voluptas atq; delectatio soler,
Ac tametsi Cæsar libro de Oratore secundo naturæ, non artis esse facetias affirmet.

page.notes: Marginal note "Sententiæ facetarum epistolarum" is set in italic and broken as "Sententiæ fa- / cetarum epi / stolarum", and is recorded as one note. The Greek terms are uncertain at many points and are marked [?]: ἀμφιβολία, εὐσχολία, παράγραμμα, παρὰ προσδοκίαν, ἐντέχνα, ἐτυμολογία, ὁμωνυμία, εἰρωνεία, ἀλληγορείας. The line "ler," at the lower right is a catchword and is also the first word of the next page. The Latin "sermonibus" in the last Latin passage and the printed "difsimulatione" were read from the scan with some doubt. The footnote above is an error on my part: no footnote is printed on this page and it should be removed. The page has no printed footnote.
